So, essentially it'd be very nice to catch that it was a 404 and just don't care about parsing the content-type or message body because it's already an invalid request based on route not matching alone.
I'd like to work on this
are there any other status codes where you would have an overlapping use case? For instance.. what about a 400?

@davidmarkclements for me, it's really about just rejecting requests from all those automated bots that try to attack & pwn literally any HTTP server on the internet, so for our use case, 404 or route not found could be a very first step: it'd allow us to kill off bot requests very early on in their lifecycle.

I'd be happy with this being a plugin too, but I don't think a plugin should use internal APIs
I think the name should be isNotFound because of parity with the serNotFoundHandler.

> what about a 400?

At that stage, the body has been already parsed (assuming the schema validation in action)

I would act in a different way, using `reply.statusCode`, since the 404 is a response domain:

In a 404 case I have
```
fastify.addHook('onRequest', (req, reply, done) => {
  console.log('onRequest', reply.statusCode) // 200
  done()
})
fastify.addHook('onResponse', (req, reply, done) => {
  console.log('onResponse', reply.statusCode) // 404
  done()
})
```

The routing should be already executed at that stage and in the `onRequest` the status code could/should (?) be already set to 404
Is there need a 404 plugin now ? if need, I will work for it 😁
No, we need a fresh PR that implements https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/2153.

@jsumners I took a brief look at the code and it seems that `Request#context` is an instance of `Context`.

https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/9d703b006bf797407d1ab50e6de6aa564fc2c0b4/lib/route.js#L233-L247

This object is not currently in the API docs. Do you suggest that the entire `Context` object be documented as part of the public API? Or instead, simply document portions of `request.context` that are relevant to a user. When I search the current docs for "context", I only find it mentioned in passing as a part of the `Reply` object.

https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blame/main/docs/Reply.md#L68-L76

It's odd, because the purpose of this PR seems to be solely about exposing `routerPath`, `routerMethod` and `is404` getter properties on `Request` by proxying these to the `context`. 

It's just a side effect that a `context` instance is now part of the public API, and I wonder if that's really what is intended since this PR did actually document what the expected API changes were. If it's intended, it's not clear what of the `Context` object should be publicly documented. If it's unintended, then it perhaps should not be documented? :shrug:
I'm confused. This PR is merged and has doc changes that show the properties added in the request documentation. What is missing in the live docs?

@jsumners that was my question! It's not clear... This change introduced a `context` property on the `Request` object. But that was not the intent of the change, and so was never documented. Back in September, when I upgraded to a version containing this change, my application broke because of this new, undocumented property. When I figured out what had happened, I came here to mention it. Three days ago, someone else came here to mention the same thing and asked for doc changes. Then you said PRs are welcome, so I figured I would do my part and look into it. But, as I've said, it's not clear what exactly should be done.

It's _sort of_ documented under https://www.fastify.io/docs/latest/Routes/#config

@mcollina posted some reasoning in another PR discussion around why we don't fully document it. But I don't recall which.
